name: Clopas
overview: Clopas is a male figure mentioned in the Gospel of John as possibly the husband of Mary, identified as Mary_3 in John 19:25. There is some scholarly suggestion that he may be the same person as Cleopas_1, though this is not definitively stated. His tribal affiliation and surname are not recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Clopas appears as a proper name in John 19:25 with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated. This name is presented plainly without additional titles or meanings in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Clopas as the husband of Mary_3, based on an inference from John 19:25. No other family relationships are explicitly documented in the biblical record beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Clopas holds significance primarily due to his possible identification as the husband of Mary present at the crucifixion of Jesus, as noted in John 19:25. This association places him in proximity to key events in the passion narrative. The potential identification with Cleopas_1, a disciple mentioned elsewhere, suggests a connection to early followers of Christ, though this remains uncertain. His mention underscores the presence of devoted followers and family members surrounding Jesus during His final moments.
